pr_title: Move clipboard operation implementations to individual editor subscreens
pr_body:
Closes #14756 by implementing [the proposal given therein](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/14756#issuecomment-957209214). This also paves the way for potentially having screen-specific clipboard functionality, like being able to copy & paste timing points. Was a pretty easy refactor and I think this came out pretty well.

The one thing I am not sure of is leaving editor-global `Clipboard` and resolving it in screens. I could move it down to the compose screen (which is the only user now), but that would mean that clipboard becomes screen-contextual. Which simplifies some things - no need to check whether data in clipboard is valid for a given screen (which is not a concern now but will become one later) - but also maybe complicates UX. Will apply the above on request.

One semi-accidental consequence of this change is that all clipboard operations are now disabled on all screens except compose. I think that makes sense, anyway - being able to copy an object on compose screen, move to timing and then paste an object in at that time via <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> is arguably a bug.
pr_comments: I actually remembered there was a second reason for leaving the `Clipboard` bindable in editor - namely the difficulty change flow and the way it preserves clipboard contents. That one is more difficult to get rid of, unfortunately...

Have also taken the liberty of unifying the existing "copy timestamp" flow in composer screen with the new screen-local clipboard flow. This makes it so copying via menu bar also will copy the timestamp out to OS, which it didn't use to do (only worked via Ctrl+C). Seemed like this pull is an appropriate place to do so anyhow.

issue_context.title: Potential cross-thread access on editor hitobject operations
issue_context.body:
Currently the editor has operations like `Paste` at a top level, while the `ComposeScreen` is loaded asynchronously, creating a `DrawableRuleset`. `DrawableRuleset` accesses hitobjects in its asynchronous load, meaning the hitobject collection could be modified:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/f8bdca542d2a6d993b3b0d4a6ddc7ae87ddaf9a4/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Editor.cs#L594

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/53c901bfa8051bab3ff96aee65ec8c16472764b3/osu.Game/Rulesets/UI/DrawableRuleset.cs#L206

As seen in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/14741/checks?check_run_id=3607664890. Not yet sure on the proper fix, just documenting the issue.
comments:
Looking into this, I think the correct path forward is to move all operations that are mutating hitobjects inside the composer (ie. `Paste` and other clipboard functionality should not exist in `Editor` in the first place, and instead be delegated to the active screen).

This will make more sense when the clipboard supports other views like design/timing.

review_comments: Wondering if it makes sense for the clipboard instance to be passed through here (and the other methods in this file) as a parameter? Should theoretically avoid any need to DI the clipboard.

It's a little dicey here because the screens will `BindValueChanged` to the clipboard content to update the availability state of all the actions, so I'd still probably feel more comfortable with DI'ing.

Unless I split `CanCut()` into methods and call that on clipboard content changes, but that feels less flexible than what is currently here (especially so that the action availability may depend on other context, like e.g. how many objects are selected - which the composer already uses).
I'm not too fussed just yet. Let's go with what is here and see how it builds out.
